title: Algebraization of affine principal rig-regular formal varieties
statement: A Noetherian adic formal scheme is a ringed space covered by finitely many $\operatorname{Spf}B$, where $B$ is a Noetherian ring complete and separated for powers of a finitely generated ideal; $\operatorname{Spf}B$ has the primes containing that ideal and the inverse-limit structure sheaf. It is reduced if its chart rings are reduced. Its reduced closed fibre is obtained by quotienting the chart rings by the radical of an ideal of definition. A formal variety in characteristic zero means such a formal scheme whose reduced closed fibre is of finite type over a characteristic-zero field [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; the field structure is not fixed as part of a morphism. In this statement the chart rings are quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. A locally principal pair $(\mathfrak X,\mathfrak I)$ has an invertible ideal of definition, locally generated by a non-zero-divisor; it is principal affine if $\mathfrak X=\operatorname{Spf}B$ and $\mathfrak I=(\pi)$ for a single non-zero-divisor $\pi\in B$. Its singular locus is cut out chartwise by the radical ideal of the nonregular locus of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The pair is rig-regular if this ideal contains a power of $\mathfrak I$. A regular morphism of pairs preserves the distinguished ideal by extension and induces regular ring maps on formal affine charts [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], that is, flat maps with Noetherian geometrically regular residue-field fibres. Let $(\mathfrak X,\mathfrak I)$ be a reduced principal affine rig-regular pair as just defined. Then there exist a characteristic-zero field $k$, a reduced finite-type $k$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and a non-zero-divisor $\pi\in A$, such that, writing $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $I=(\pi)$, the pair $(\mathfrak X,\mathfrak I)$ is isomorphic to $(\operatorname{Spf}\widehat A_I,I\widehat A_I)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and $X_{\mathrm{sing}}\subseteq V(I)$. Such an affine finite-type pair with principal invertible ideal and singular locus contained in its closed fibre is called an Elkik pair. A finite ordered tower of ordinary blowups of $X$ whose centers lie over $V(I)$ completes, with the same extended center ideals and their order, to the corresponding formal blowup tower of $\mathfrak X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup, pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Temkin arXiv:0904.1592v2, §§3.1.1–3.1.4, Remark 3.1.3(ii), Remark 3.1.4(i)–(iii), §3.3.1 and first sentence of §3.4.1 (printed pp.17–18,21,25); formal blowup completion is §2.4.5. Elkik algebraization supplies the principal pair regular away from its closed fibre. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak X=\operatorname{Spf}B$, with distinguished generator $\pi$. Choose the characteristic-zero field $k$ over which $B/\sqrt{\pi B}$ is finite type. Apply [lem-per-principal-formal-coefficient-presentation] to obtain a lift $k\to B$ and a surjection $P=\widehat{k[t,x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_{(t)}\twoheadrightarrow B$, sending $t$ to $\pi$. Put $J=\ker(P\to B)$; then $P/J=B$. This identifies the chosen principal ideal, not just its radical.

Let $K$ be the radical ideal defining the nonregular locus of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Rig-regularity says $\pi^N\in K$ for some $N$. If a prime does not contain $\pi$, it cannot contain $K$, so its local ring is regular; hence $B[1/\pi]$ is regular by the definition of regularity. Apply [lem-per-regular-generic-continuous-jacobian] to the presentation of Step 1. It yields $c\geq0$ and $h:B^{\oplus r}\to J/J^2$ with $h\delta=t^c\operatorname{id}$. For $a\in(t)^c\subseteq k[t]$, write $a=t^cu$ and set $h_a=uh$; then $h_a\delta=a\operatorname{id}$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 proof and Proposition 3.3.2; Non_Embedded_Desingularization Remark 3.1.4(ii).

proof.text: The field $k$ is excellent by [lem-exc-fields-excellent]. Since $R=k[t]$ is finite type over $k$, [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] makes $R$ excellent, hence a Noetherian G-ring by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. The power-splitting identities of Step 2 and the given completeness of $B$ therefore satisfy [lem-per-g-ring-rig-smooth-algebraization] with base $R$ and ideal $(t)$. Obtain a finite type $R$-algebra $C$ and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat C_{(t)}\cong B$. In particular $C$ is finite type over $k$: its finitely many $R$-generators together with $t$ generate it over $k$.

source.place: Tags 0GAJ (lemma-equivalent-with-artin-smooth) and 0GAT (proposition-approximate); the latter supplies the G-ring version of the Elkik algebraization used by Temkin.

proof.text: Again [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] makes $C$ excellent, so it is quasi-excellent by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Its completion is the reduced ring $B$, with $t=\pi$ a non-zero-divisor and $B[1/t]$ regular by Step 2. Apply [lem-per-principal-completion-good-neighborhood] to choose $g\in1+tC$ and put $A=C_g$. This is finite type over $k$, generated by generators of $C$ and $g^{-1}$ with relation $gg^{-1}=1$. It is reduced, $t$ is a non-zero-divisor, and $A[1/t]$ is regular. Its completion identifies with $B$ preserving $t$, hence preserves the distinguished principal ideal. Renaming $t$ as $\pi$, the regularity of $A[1/\pi]$ means exactly $X_{\mathrm{sing}}\subseteq V(\pi)$ for $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.5 and shrinking in Theorem 3.4.1; Non_Embedded_Desingularization §3.4.1 first sentence.

proof.text: For the tower clause use [lem-per-supported-formal-blowup-algebraization]. Its hypotheses hold: $A$ is finite type over the characteristic-zero field $k$, hence excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], and $V(\pi)$ is a coherent closed subscheme on this Noetherian scheme. At each Noetherian level a center lying over $V(\pi)$ has ideal $L$ with $\pi\in\sqrt L$, hence $\pi^e\in L$ for some $e$. Thus the given finite tower is supported in precisely the sense of the cited correspondence. Completing it gives the corresponding ordered formal tower with the same extended center ideals. Apply the fixed identification $\widehat X_{V(\pi)}\cong\mathfrak X$; every retained center and its order are preserved. This also covers the length-zero tower and empty centers.
